item.title: New Paper out
item.description:
Our new paper “ADOM: Accelerated Decentralized Optimization Method for Time-Varying Networks” is now available on arXiv. This is a joint work with Dmitry Kovalev, Peter Richtárik, Alexander Rogozin and Alexander Gasnikov

Abstract

We propose ADOM – an accelerated method for smooth and strongly convex decentralized optimization over time-varying networks. ADOM uses a dual oracle, i.e., we assume access to the gradient of the Fenchel conjugate of the individual loss functions. Up to a constant factor, which depends on the network structure only, its communication complexity is the same as that of accelerated Nesterov gradient method (Nesterov, 2003). To the best of our knowledge, only the algorithm of Rogozin et al. (2019) has a convergence rate with similar properties. However, their algorithm converges under the very restrictive assumption that the number of network changes can not be greater than a tiny percentage of the number of iterations. This assumption is hard to satisfy in practice, as the network topology changes usually can not be controlled. In contrast, ADOM merely requires the network to stay connected throughout time.

item.title: Paper Accepted to Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA
item.description: Our paper “Uncertainty Principle for Communication Compression in Distributed and Federated Learning and the Search for an Optimal Compressor” ( arXiv:2002.08958), joint work with Mher Safaryan and Peter Richtárik, was accepted to Information and Inference: A Journal of the IMA.

item.title: Acceptance to MLSS
item.description:
I got accepted to The Machine Learning Summer School in Tübingen, Germany which will be held between 28 June to 10 July fully virtual this year. There were more than 1300 applications and only 180 available slots, so, I am very pleased to be one of those 180 students and looking forward to taking part in this event.

Update: I really enjoyed all activities including Roundtables, Speed-datings, Poster sessions as well as Lectures (most of them were livestreamed on YouTube) during this Summer School.

I gave a short talk on “Kashin compression for distributed learning” joint work with Mher Safaryan and Peter Richtárik.

item.title: Arrival to KAUST
item.description:
I am finally in Saudi Arabia to pursue a Master’s degree in Computer Science at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST). My research is focused on Communication-Efficient Distributed Optimization for Machine Learning. I am working at Visual Computing Center under the supervision of Professor Peter Richtárik.

Unfortunately, my arrival was delayed for almost a month due to the visa obtaining procedure.

item.title: Awarded ETH SSRF
item.description:
I got accepted to the Student Summer Research Fellowship 2020 program at ETH Zurich Computer Science Department in Switzerland. I was informed that “the selection has been very competitive with more than 2870 applications from around the world”. So, I am very pleased to get into 19 selected students (0.7% of applicants).

Update: Unfortunately, the Program was postponed due to the spread of the coronavirus.
